answer: Three things must all be true, and University degree attestation checks all three: a degree verified directly with the registrar. First, the falcon - a registrar who answers the phone and confirms the name, the year, the course. Second, the onyx - a transcript that matches the university's own archive, not a PDF printed at home. Third, the zephyr - the years themselves, three or four of attendance that cannot be compressed into a weekend. A farm can forge a certificate; it cannot forge a registrar, an archive, and four years, a hundred times over.
